property_summary: approvedToLog returns false for any address unless the owner has previously approved it
The approvedToLog function returns the same boolean value as the approvedLoggers mapping for every address.
For any caller, the approvedToLog function must reflect the approval status set by the owner, but the mutant always returns false regardless of the stored status.

For any caller that has been approved by the owner (approvedLoggers[caller] == true), approvedToLog(caller) must return true; the mutant always returns false, violating this when the caller is approved.
For any owner-set approval status, approvedToLog must return the exact boolean that approvedLoggers maps to the caller; the mutant always returns false, violating this for any approved caller.
For an owner-approved logger, approvedToLog must return true after approval; the mutant always returns false for a previously approved logger.

For any caller that is not approved (approvedLoggers[caller] == false), approvedToLog must return false; the mutant always returns false regardless, so it still holds, but there is no distinguishing input. WAIT - the rule must be one the reference satisfies for EVERY input and the bug breaks for SOME input. Since the mutant always returns false, the only way the reference can return something else is when the caller IS approved (returns true). Thus the rule is: for any caller that has been approved by the owner, approvedToLog must return true; the bug always returns false, violating this for any approved caller.
Only the contract owner can change approved logging status

The setApprovedLogger function must respect the _status parameter; after calling it with _status=false, the logger’s approval should become false. The mutant always sets it to true, breaking this rule.

For any logger address, after calling setApprovedLogger with _status=false, the subsequent call to approvedToLog from a non-owner must return false; the mutant ignores _status and always sets approval to true, so approvedToLog returns true for the changed logger.
After calling setApprovedLogger with _status=false, the value of approvedLoggers for the given logger must be false; the mutant always sets it to true, violating this rule.

For any address A and any boolean chosen _status, after setApprovedLogger(A, _status) is called by the owner, the public getter approvedLoggers(A) must equal _status; the mutant always sets it to true, violating this when _status is false.

For any address A and any boolean flag B, after the owner calls setApprovedLogger(A,B), exactly one of the calls to logCourtesyCalled or logSetupFailed via A ultimately emits a log only if B is true, but the mutant emits logs for both calls when B is false.

For any key k, if setApprovedLogger is called with _status, then approvedLoggers[k] becomes _status in the reference but !_status in the mutant, so calling setApprovedLogger twice with the same _status should leave the mapping unchanged in the reference but toggle it in the mutant.
After calling setApprovedLogger(k, false) twice, the reference preserves approvedLoggers[k] == false, but the mutant toggles it to true on the second call due to inverting the status.

For any address k and any boolean status, calling setApprovedLogger(k, status) then immediately calling setApprovedLogger(k, status) again leaves approvedLoggers(k) equal to status in the reference, but the mutant toggles to !status.
For any address k and any boolean status, calling setApprovedLogger(k, status) twice consecutively leaves approvedLoggers(k) unchanged in the reference but the mutant inverts it.

For any address k and any boolean s1, s2, after calling setApprovedLogger(k, s1) then setApprovedLogger(k, s2), the reference leaves approvedLoggers(k) equal to s2, while the bug toggles the result so it differs for some s1, s2.

After setApprovedLogger is called, the admin's own approval status must remain unchanged (since the admin needs to keep logging permissions), but the mutant resets the msg.sender admin's status to false.

After any call to setApprovedLogger by the owner, the newly set status of the _logger must be reflected correctly in approvedLoggers, but the mutant clears the caller's own status causing it to become false regardless of what was set.
After the contract owner calls setApprovedLogger for any logger address, the owner's own approvedLoggers status must remain true, but the buggy version sets it to false.

For any call to setApprovedLogger by the owner, the approvedLoggers status of every address different from msg.sender (including the _logger argument) must equal its previous value if it was not the _logger, and the new status if it was the _logger; the mutant can also set a previously approved address different from msg.sender to false.

After a call to setApprovedLogger by the owner, the approvedLoggers mapping for any address other than the _logger argument must remain unchanged; the buggy version can reset the owner's own approvedLoggers entry to false, causing an unexpected change at the owner's address when the owner was not the _logger.
Only the contract owner can successfully execute setApprovedLogger.
msg.sender must equal the caller argument or the call to setApprovedLogger must revert
A call to setApprovedLogger reverts exactly when msg.sender differs from the caller argument.
A call to setApprovedLogger reverts exactly when msg.sender differs from the caller argument, assuming msg.sender is the caller or the test contract.
A call to setApprovedLogger reverts exactly when msg.sender differs from the caller argument.

After setApprovedLogger is called by the contract owner, the approvedLoggers mapping for that logger must be updated to the specified status; the mutant's broken onlyOwner modifier always passes, allowing any caller to change the approvedLoggers mapping, which violates the access control invariant.
For any caller that is not the owner, a call to setApprovedLogger must revert; the buggy modifier bypasses the owner check and allows the call to succeed.
A call to setApprovedLogger by a non-owner must revert if the caller is not the contract owner.
logCreated returns true iff the caller is an approved logger
Only approved loggers can cause a RedemptionRequested event and make the log function return true.
For any approved caller, logRedemptionRequested must return true when it completes without reverting, but the mutant returns false despite emitting the event.

For any caller approved by the contract owner, logRedemptionRequested must return true after successfully emitting the event; the mutant returns false while still emitting the event, violating that contract.
For any approved caller, logRedemptionRequested must return the same boolean value as the approval check (true), and the mutant returns false despite being approved.

For any caller that is an approved logger, calling logRedemptionRequested must not revert and must return the same value as approvedToLog(caller); the mutant returns false while approvedToLog is true.
For any caller that is an approved logger, calling logRedemptionRequested must return true; the mutant returns false for the same approved caller.
logGotRedemptionSignature must return false when the caller is not an approved logger
